headline: High-risk default data exfiltration and cascading misuse: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools while Airbyte has broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can ingest files and MCP/tool outputs, and Airbyte can emit data over broad network egress. If Airbyte-produced content is routed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins, attacker-controlled payloads could steer tool use. The shared path is plausible from the profiles, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs
IF Semantic Kernel parses Airbyte-produced files as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict content separator before passing Airbyte output to Semantic Kernel
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files for the shared workflow
Require human review of any Airbyte-derived text before tool execution
Use allowlisted schemas for plugin inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Semantic Kernel reads/writes files and can call external model providers and MCP/OpenAPI tools. In a shared workspace, data can flow from Airbyte into Semantic Kernel and then out to third parties, creating a realistic leakage path in default-style deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or file handoff
IF Semantic Kernel forwards loaded context to external model providers or MCP/OpenAPI tools
mitigations: Restrict the shared directory to non-sensitive samples
Turn off automatic file ingestion in the Semantic Kernel workflow
Block outbound calls from the shared run until review completes
Separate credentials for Airbyte and Semantic Kernel
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on handoff files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and has broad egress, while Semantic Kernel can write files and invoke MCP/OpenAPI tools. Their write surfaces overlap on shared mutable resources if orchestrated together, but Airbyte does not advertise filesystem write and Semantic Kernel does not advertise git modification, so the strongest conflict indicators are not met.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined files
IF an MCP plugin mutates shared state without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use per-run locks on shared files
Disable write access for one agent in the shared path
Serialize tool calls that mutate the same resource
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs, while Airbyte produces data that may be treated as authoritative upstream facts. If Airbyte output is fed into Semantic Kernel without verification, the orchestrator can propagate bad data into downstream actions or model calls, making cascading errors likely.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is used as authoritative input to Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel triggers downstream actions from that input without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step between extraction and orchestration
Require source checksums for Airbyte outputs
Limit Semantic Kernel to read-only summarization on first pass
Log and review all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add typed contracts for inter-agent handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, and Semantic Kernel handles application context plus model-provider credentials. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through Semantic Kernel’s external model providers or MCP/OpenAPI tools, retention and jurisdiction controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the higher defensible severity.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated or residency-bound records
IF Semantic Kernel sends that data to external model providers or plugins with different retention rules
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Route regulated data only to approved providers
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and outputs
Review retention settings for each provider
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
